_about: Minari, the carved-statue game on the Playground (/playground/#minari), issue #131. What the series says about Minari is in Legacy/Behind The Scenes/World Lore/Sports, Games and Passtime.md (Minari), Vol 1 Ch II (the game table), Vol 1 Epilogue, Vol 3 Ch II and IV, and the Arc #2 notes (Book 6 Ch 3); see content/qa/minari.md. The game's rules beyond that are Deo's answers on #131 (2026-11-23): play against the computer (Nina easy, Aurora medium, Neferteri challenging); statues are Races, Fauna and Beasts, and the creature a statue shows is its strength; Flora are bases that help or hurt the statue on them; terrain squares (type and height, from the World Lore and the world map) give bonuses, like MTG's colours plus height; painting is cosmetic; each player hides the nari stone in one of their own statues; no dialogue. Every number below was set by Claude from the World Lore (size, danger, soul energy skills, habitat altitude) and rebalanced for play; 'why' says where each came from. Names, pictures and lore links come from the World Lore pages through the build, never retyped here: each 'name' must match an entry title.

rules._why: Gwent-like (the lore's 'like Gwent'): best of three rounds ('the final round', Arc #2). 10 statues and 4 bases must last the whole match, so every piece played is spent, as in Gwent. A lane's losers are eliminated and revealed (the lore's goal: 'eliminate the true version'; Vol 3's 'fog of war').

terrains._why: Lower plains and grasslands (most Fauna habitats), Buhraies Plains, Aldemeri
Dense forests of the south, Freeish, Blood City, Woodland
Ponds, lakes (Lukewarm, Sweetlake), swamps from Sanbi to Tastyleaf, the oceans and deltas
The desert of Gandew (Sayna, Sand Worms, Lolish)
Whiteland and the snow mountains of Fuhrair
Hifuna and Bahyum: radioactive leftovers and Walking Heart stones (Lands: Hifuna, Bahyum)

heights._why: Habitat altitudes in Flora (~0 km, ~0-1 km, ~1-2 km, ~2-4 km) and the 2 km cliff of the Buhraies Plains (Lands). 0 = lowland, 1 = up to ~2 km, 2 = mountains, ~2-4 km.
